question: A marketing coordinator's first attempt at a campaign brief comes back disappointing. She wants to improve the result on her next attempt. What should she do first?
options: A) Rewrite her request at much greater length, since more description generally produces a more considered answer.
B) Send the same request again, on the basis that a second attempt often produces a noticeably better result.
C) Work out what is actually wrong with the answer, since a vague ask and missing material need different fixes.
D) Break the brief into four smaller requests, so that each part of the campaign is handled on its own terms.
correct_answers: C) Work out what is actually wrong with the answer, since a vague ask and missing material need different fixes.
explanations: Length is not the variable. A longer version of an unclear request is still unclear, and padding can bury the one instruction that mattered.
Resending an unchanged request repeats the conditions that produced the weak answer, so any improvement is chance rather than a fix.

Correct. The causes call for opposite responses: a vague ask needs a tighter specification, missing source material needs the material supplied, and a wrong task needs restating. Changing something before knowing which it is means guessing.
Splitting up helps when a request is genuinely doing too much, but applied blindly it produces four requests carrying the same original flaw.
